manifesto: The primary virtue of a cleaning tool is not simply freeing disk space, but ensuring no developer source code or personal data is ever damaged. Dev Cleaner adheres strictly to these rules:
All operations dispatch items via the native Windows Shell COM API to the Recycle Bin. Users can restore any folder in one click at any time.
Symlinks and NTFS Junction points are strictly excluded during scan and deletion. Any reparse point pointing outside the project tree (such as C:\\Windows or ~/.ssh) is immediately blocked.
If an active Node.js, Cargo, or IDE process holds a lock on a target folder, Dev Cleaner never forces deletion; it safely skips the target and reports it in the summary.

mcp-tools: MCP Tools
Dev Cleaner MCP Tools Reference
The Dev Cleaner MCP server exposes 8 tools: 6 standard tools plus 2 destructive tools that are hidden unless the server runs with --allow-destructive.
1. `devcleaner_scan_workspace`
Scans the workspace and yields cleanable candidates as structured JSON.
2. `devcleaner_preview_cleanup`
Builds a cleanup plan, returns a single-use token and never deletes anything.
3. `devcleaner_clean_safe` (deprecated alias)
Deprecated alias of devcleaner_preview_cleanup. It only previews a plan and never deletes anything; use preview_cleanup plus execute_cleanup.
4. `devcleaner_list_caches`
Reports cache metrics for 21 developer tools and package managers.
5. `devcleaner_get_history`
Returns historical records of previous cleanup operations.
6. `devcleaner_inspect_target`
Inspects safety rules and classifications for a specific path.
7. `devcleaner_execute_cleanup` (destructive)
Executes a previously previewed plan. Requires confirm:true, a single-use token, --allow-destructive and the MCP destructive setting.
8. `devcleaner_clean_cache` (destructive)
Invokes official package manager CLI commands to purge cache. Requires confirm:true, --allow-destructive and the MCP destructive setting.

webhook-schema: Standard JSON payload dispatched to the webhook target upon completion:

Field reference event is always scan or clean . The legacy names scan_completed and cleanup_completed are accepted as aliases and are rewritten to the canonical names before delivery. timestamp , product and version identify the installation that raised the event; the payload is never signed. status is success , partial (the scan stopped early) or cancelled (the user pressed Stop). total_bytes is the reclaimable space that was measured; total_human is its formatted form. cleaned_count and cleaned_bytes only appear on cleanup events. Scan events also carry scan_id , root_path , duration_ms and, when the result is partial, stop_reason . Cleanup events from the desktop app also carry plan_id , mode , success_count , error_count , moved_bytes and reclaim_bytes . )}
